as_told.title: Project Sign Estimate of the Situation rejected by Vandenberg

plain: The story is that Project Sign, the US Air Force's first UFO study, written at Wright Field in Ohio, concluded that UFOs were spacecraft from other worlds. Its staff are said to have set this out in a top secret report called the Estimate of the Situation, dated by the record to 1948. The report then went to General Hoyt Vandenberg, the head of the Air Force, and the story says he had it burned. If true, the Air Force's own experts reached that conclusion early and it was buried from the top. Michels tells it himself, saying that 'in 1949 Sign personnel wrote a top secret report concluding UFOs were extraterrestrial craft.' A former Air Force officer named Robert Salas also tells it. He dates it to 1948 and insists, 'It was a real document. It was seen by Ruppelt.' He means Edward J. Ruppelt, who later led the Air Force's UFO work and wrote The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, published in 1956, which Salas cites as his source. In Salas's version, Vandenberg rejected the Estimate rather than burning it, and the two tellers differ by a year on its date.
